work.title: Case studies
work.lead: Four real products, told through the problem they solved, the technical calls I made and what shipped in the end.

modest-pos.title: Modest POS
modest-pos.summary: A SaaS point of sale with AI-driven cross-sell recommendations, built for small businesses across Latin America.
modest-pos.problem: Small food businesses leave margin on the table with every order: the cashier has no time to suggest add-ons, and the POS systems on the market are either expensive or demand integrations and a PCI scope a small shop cannot take on.
modest-pos.solution: I built a complete point of sale in Next.js on top of Supabase — Postgres, auth and storage — with a register, a catalogue with costs and margins, stock control, a live order board and a self-service kiosk. Subscriptions are billed through PayPal and the whole thing deploys to Vercel. The recommendation engine learns from the merchant's actual menu and answers on a single endpoint; if the AI does not respond in time it falls back to best sellers, so the screen never freezes. Only product IDs and prices travel, which keeps the system entirely out of PCI-DSS scope.
modest-pos.result: A multi-tenant SaaS in production with a free trial, real-time analytics, billing and no-code onboarding. It stands on its own — there is no other POS behind it.

screen-notify.title: Screen Notify
screen-notify.summary: An Android app in Flutter that turns the notifications that matter into fullscreen alerts, with rules per app and per contact.
screen-notify.role: Mobile development, native layer and monetisation
screen-notify.problem: An important notification gets buried under dozens of daily alerts. Existing alerting apps cannot tell who is writing or which app it came from, and they stop working exactly when they are needed most: with the phone locked or the app killed.
screen-notify.solution: A hybrid architecture. Flutter handles the interface, the rules, local storage and purchase state; a native Kotlin layer runs a NotificationListenerService that intercepts system notifications, matches them against the rule database in real time and launches fullscreen alerts even when the device is locked or the app is not in memory. Rules filter by application and by contact, with separate triggers for messages and calls.
screen-notify.result: A published app monetised through RevenueCat subscriptions and AdMob. The rule schema has been through four iterations with automatic backward migration, so no update has ever broken a user's configuration, and a triple guard — reactive in Dart, proactive on boot and defensive in Kotlin — keeps premium state consistent even offline.

enterprise-employee-system.title: Enterprise Employee System
enterprise-employee-system.summary: A corporate workforce management platform on .NET 8 and Angular, deployed to Azure with CI/CD and observability.
enterprise-employee-system.problem: Managing a large workforce from spreadsheets does not scale: no combined filters, no traceability when something breaks, and nobody hears about an error until a user reports it themselves.
enterprise-employee-system.solution: A .NET 8 API with Entity Framework Core and an Angular frontend using Material Design. The dashboard resolves pagination, sorting and multi-criteria filtering on the server rather than in the browser. An HTTP interceptor centralises user-facing errors and a global handler logs them to Application Insights; on a 500 the system fires an alert to the technical team instead of waiting for someone to notice.
enterprise-employee-system.result: Deployed to Azure App Service and Static Web Apps through a multi-stage GitHub Actions pipeline: backend quality gate, frontend build with environment injection and parallel deploy. Every secret lives in Azure app settings and GitHub Secrets — nothing sensitive reaches the repository.

the-roulette-game.title: The Roulette Game
the-roulette-game.summary: A browser-playable casino roulette with real betting logic and persistence, built as a technical assessment on a fixed stack.
the-roulette-game.problem: A technical assessment with the stack decided up front: reproduce casino roulette with bets on colour, odd/even and a specific number, getting the payout logic and history persistence right.
the-roulette-game.solution: A Vue 3 frontend with TypeScript and Pinia holding the table state, the bets and the balance; a .NET backend with SQL Server to resolve each spin, calculate payouts per bet type and persist the history. All packaged with Docker so it comes up with a single command.
the-roulette-game.result: A complete, deployable game with the betting logic covered and a clean split between the client-side simulation and the authoritative server-side resolution.

about.title: About me
about.lead: Full-stack developer based in the Dominican Republic, working with teams and clients at home and abroad.

bio.p1: I started in 2020 building e-commerce storefronts, with an obsession for understanding how things work underneath. Six years on the obsession is unchanged — the difference is that the projects now reach production and have users depending on them.
bio.p2: I'm comfortable at both ends: I'll drop into a native Kotlin layer to intercept system notifications, and in the same month set up an Azure deployment pipeline or design the data model for a multi-tenant SaaS. What doesn't change is the judgement — I'd rather ship a boring solution people understand than an elegant one nobody can maintain.
bio.p3: Today I'm the founder of RCDL APPS, where I build my own products — Screen Notify and Modest POS — while taking on consulting work across backend, mobile and cloud.

items.2020: First years as a fullstack web developer at Softver: e-commerce storefronts, Stripe integration and headless CMS.
items.2023: Backend .NET at Meditod, building endpoints and modules for an ERP with a focus on security and performance.
items.2025: Frontend at Insoltech for a financial-sector platform, optimising performance and accessibility.
items.2026: Semi-senior fullstack at Kleio Inc. with Angular 19 (SSR, NgRx) and ASP.NET Core 8 microservices on Azure. Alongside that I launched Screen Notify and Modest POS under RCDL APPS.
